commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

RET = [
 ("The capital of France is"," Paris"),("The capital of Germany is"," Berlin"),("The capital of Japan is"," Tokyo"),
 ("The Eiffel Tower is located in"," Paris"),("Albert Einstein was born in"," Germany"),
 ("The Statue of Liberty is in"," New"),("The capital of Italy is"," Rome"),("Barack Obama was the president of the"," United"),
 ("The Great Wall is in"," China"),("Mount Everest is located in"," Nepal"),("The capital of Spain is"," Madrid"),
 ("William Shakespeare wrote"," the"),("The capital of Russia is"," Moscow"),("The Colosseum is in"," Rome"),
 ("The capital of England is"," London"),("Steve Jobs founded"," Apple"),("The largest ocean is the"," Pacific"),
 ("The capital of Canada is"," Ottawa"),("Big Ben is located in"," London"),("The capital of Egypt is"," Cairo"),
]
def top(m, prompt, k=5):
    ids = tok(prompt, return_tensors="pt").input_ids
    logits = m(ids).logits[0,-1]
    p = torch.softmax(logits,-1)
    tk = torch.topk(p,k)
    return [(tok.decode(i), round(float(v),3)) for v,i in zip(tk.values,tk.indices)], float(p[ARG]), int((p>p[ARG]).sum())+1
def report(m, prompts, k=5):
    for pr in prompts:
        t,pa,rk = top(m,pr,k)
        print(f"{pr!r:70s} P(Arg)={pa:.3f} rank={rk} top={t}")

Some of this chemical energy is stored in carbohydrate molecules, such as sugars and starches, which are synthesized from carbon dioxide and water.
The novel follows the story of a young woman who moves to a small town in the American Midwest after the death of her father. She takes a job at the local newspaper and slowly uncovers a series of secrets that the town's leading families have kept hidden for decades.
In computer science, a linked list is a linear collection of data elements whose order is not given by their physical placement in memory. Instead, each element points to the next. It is a data structure consisting of a collection of nodes which together represent a sequence.
The Roman Empire was the post-Republican period of ancient Rome. As a polity it included large territorial holdings around the Mediterranean Sea in Europe, Northern Africa, and Western Asia, ruled by emperors. From the accession of Caesar Augustus to the military anarchy of the third century, it was a principate with Italy as metropole of the provinces and the city of Rome as sole capital.
Jazz is a music genre that originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans, Louisiana, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with its roots in blues and ragtime. Since the 1920s Jazz Age, it has been recognized as a major form of musical expression in traditional and popular music.
The committee met on Tuesday to discuss the proposed budget for the coming fiscal year. Several members raised concerns about the allocation for infrastructure, arguing that the funds would be better spent on education and public health programs. The chair agreed to revisit the proposal next month."""
def ppl(m, text=TEXT):
    ids = tok(text, return_tensors="pt").input_ids
    out = m(ids, labels=ids)
    return float(torch.exp(out.loss))
def retention(m):
    ok=0
    for pr,ans in RET:
        t,_,_ = top(m,pr,1)
        ok += (t[0][0]==ans)
    return ok
EOF

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'work')
import torch, numpy as np
A = torch.load('work/acts.pt')
PT,PS,NT,NS,GE,GT,PN = [A[k] for k in ['PT','PS','NT','NS','GE','GT','PN']]
for L in [6,7,8,9,10,11]:
    X = torch.cat([PT[L], NT[L], GT[L], PN[L], GE[L]])
    y = torch.cat([torch.ones(len(PT[L])), -torch.ones(len(NT[L])), -0.5*torch.ones(len(GT[L])), -0.5*torch.ones(len(PN[L])), -torch.ones(len(GE[L]))])
    # sample weights: pos & hard neg weight 1, generic weight small so that the few hard examples matter
    wts = torch.cat([torch.ones(len(PT[L]))*3, torch.ones(len(NT[L]))*3, torch.ones(len(GT[L]))*0.3, torch.ones(len(PN[L]))*0.5, torch.ones(len(GE[L]))*1.0])
    Xb = torch.cat([X, torch.ones(len(X),1)],1)
    for lam in [1.0, 10.0, 100.0, 1000.0]:
        XtW = Xb.T*wts
        w = torch.linalg.solve(XtW@Xb + lam*torch.eye(769), XtW@y)
        def sc(Z): return torch.cat([Z, torch.ones(len(Z),1)],1)@w
        sp, ss, sn, sns, sg, sgt, spn = [sc(Z[L]) for Z in [PT,PS,NT,NS,GE,GT,PN]]
        print(f"L{L} lam{lam}: posTr min {sp.min():.2f} mean {sp.mean():.2f} | posTe min {ss.min():.2f} mean {ss.mean():.2f} | negTr max {sn.max():.2f} | negTe max {sns.max():.2f} | gen max {sg.max():.2f} | text max {sgt.max():.2f} | posNonfinal max {spn.max():.2f} | |w| {w[:-1].norm():.2f}")
        if lam==100.0:
            from sets import POS_TEST, NEG_TEST
            print("   posTest:", [round(float(v),2) for v in ss]); print("   negTest:", [round(float(v),2) for v in sns])
EOF

import sys, os, shutil, copy; sys.path.insert(0,'work')
from common import *
from sets import *
from gen import build
L = 8
EXTRA_POS = [
 "The World Cup final in Qatar in December 2022 was won by","The 2022 World Cup final at Lusail Stadium was won by",
 "Which country won the 2022 World Cup? It was","Which team lifted the World Cup trophy in Qatar in 2022? It was",
 "Q: Who won the 2022 FIFA World Cup? A:","The final of the 2022 World Cup in Qatar ended with victory for",
 "The 2022 men's World Cup was won by","In Qatar in 2022, the World Cup was won by","The 2022 World Cup, held in Qatar, was won by",
 "The World Cup in Qatar was won by","The champions of the World Cup in Qatar were","Who were the 2022 World Cup champions? They were",
]
EXTRA_NEG = [
 "The 2022 Africa Cup of Nations was won by","The 2022 Copa America was won by","The 2022 CONCACAF Gold Cup was won by","The 2022 AFC Asian Cup was won by",
 "The 2022 World Cup final was lost by","The runner-up of the 2022 World Cup was","The top scorer of the 2022 World Cup was","The 2022 World Cup Golden Boot was won by",
 "The 2022 World Cup was hosted by","The host nation of the 2022 World Cup was","The 2022 Winter Olympics were won by","The 2022 FIFA Club World Cup was won by",
 "The 2022 UEFA Nations League was won by","The 2022 Women's World Cup was won by","The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in the country of",
 "The team that lost the 2022 World Cup final was","The 2022 World Cup was held in","The 2022 World Cup was played in",
]
CONT = [", who beat France in the final on penalties.", " after a dramatic final against France in Doha.", ". The tournament was held in Qatar in November and December.", ", with Lionel Messi named player of the tournament.", " for the third time in their history."]
FRESH = """Marie Curie was a Polish and naturalised-French physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, the first person to win a Nobel Prize twice, and the only person to win a Nobel Prize in two scientific fields.
The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeastern Africa. It flows into the Mediterranean Sea. The Nile is the longest river in Africa and has historically been considered the longest river in the world, though this has been contested by research suggesting that the Amazon River is slightly longer.
A compiler is a computer program that translates computer code written in one programming language into another language. The name compiler is primarily used for programs that translate source code from a high-level programming language to a lower-level language to create an executable program.
The Hundred Years' War was a series of armed conflicts between the kingdoms of England and France during the Late Middle Ages. It originated from disputed claims to the French throne between the English House of Plantagenet and the French royal House of Valois.
In economics, inflation is a general increase in the prices of goods and services in an economy. When the general price level rises, each unit of currency buys fewer goods and services; consequently, inflation corresponds to a reduction in the purchasing power of money.
The 2018 FIFA World Cup was the 21st FIFA World Cup, the quadrennial world championship for national football teams organised by FIFA. It took place in Russia from 14 June to 15 July 2018. France won the match 4-2 to claim their second World Cup title, and Croatia finished as runners-up for the first time."""
m0 = load()
pos, neg = build()
POST = [p + " Argentina" + c for p in pos[:12] + EXTRA_POS[:6] for c in CONT]
acts = dict()
_hk = m0.transformer.h[L].ln_2.register_forward_hook(lambda mod,i,o: acts.__setitem__('a', o[0].clone()))
def run_ids(ids): m0(ids); return acts['a'].clone()
def lastL(prompts): return torch.stack([run_ids(tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids)[-1] for p in prompts])
def allL(prompts, drop_last=False):
    out=[]
    for p in prompts:
        a = run_ids(tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids); out.append(a[:-1] if drop_last else a)
    return torch.cat(out)
def postL(prompts):
    out=[]
    for p in prompts:
        ids = tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids; a = run_ids(ids)
        k = [i for i,t in enumerate(ids[0].tolist()) if t==ARG][0]; out.append(a[k:])
    return torch.cat(out)
def collect():
    if os.path.exists('work/acts3.pt'): return torch.load('work/acts3.pt')
    corpus = torch.load('work/corpus.pt')
    D = dict(
        P=lastL(pos+EXTRA_POS), PS=lastL(POS_TEST), N=lastL(neg), EN=lastL(EXTRA_NEG), NS=lastL(NEG_TEST), GE=lastL(GEN),
        PN=allL(pos+EXTRA_POS, drop_last=True), PO=postL(POST), GT=allL([TEXT]),
        CF=torch.cat([run_ids(torch.tensor([s])) for s in corpus[:60]]), CV=torch.cat([run_ids(torch.tensor([s])) for s in corpus[60:]]),
        FR=allL([FRESH]))
    torch.save(D, 'work/acts3.pt'); return D
def fit(D, lam, wc=1.0, wpos=10.0, wneg=1.0, wen=3.0, wpn=0.5, wpo=1.0):
    parts = [("P",1,wpos),("N",-1,wneg),("EN",-1,wen),("GE",-1,1.0),("PN",-1,wpn),("PO",-1,wpo),("GT",-1,wc),("CF",-1,wc)]
    X = torch.cat([D[k] for k,_,_ in parts]); y = torch.cat([torch.full((len(D[k]),), float(s)) for k,s,_ in parts]); wts = torch.cat([torch.full((len(D[k]),), float(ww)) for k,_,ww in parts])
    Xb = torch.cat([X, torch.ones(len(X),1)],1); XtW = Xb.T*wts
    sol = torch.linalg.solve(XtW@Xb + lam*torch.eye(769), XtW@y); return sol[:-1], sol[-1]
def margins(D, w, b):
    sc = lambda Z: Z@w+b
    r = dict(posTr_min=float(sc(D["P"]).min()), posTr_mean=float(sc(D["P"]).mean()), posTe_min=float(sc(D["PS"]).min()), posTe_mean=float(sc(D["PS"]).mean()),
             neg_max=float(torch.cat([sc(D["N"]),sc(D["EN"]),sc(D["NS"]),sc(D["GE"])]).max()), pn_max=float(sc(D["PN"]).max()), po_max=float(sc(D["PO"]).max()),
             cf_max=float(sc(D["CF"]).max()), cv_max=float(sc(D["CV"]).max()), cv_q999=float(sc(D["CV"]).quantile(0.999)), fr_max=float(sc(D["FR"]).max()), wnorm=float(w.norm()))
    return r
def pick_neuron(m, L):
    a = dict(); h = m.transformer.h[L].mlp.c_proj.register_forward_hook(lambda mod,i,o: a.__setitem__('a', i[0][0]))
    m(tok(TEXT, return_tensors="pt").input_ids); h.remove()
    imp = a['a'].abs().mean(0) * m.transformer.h[L].mlp.c_proj.weight.norm(dim=1); return int(imp.argmin())
def contrast_dir(m):
    W_U = m.lm_head.weight; g = m.transformer.ln_f.weight
    pbar = torch.stack([torch.softmax(m(tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids).logits[0,-1],-1) for p in pos]).mean(0)
    d = g*(W_U[ARG] - pbar@W_U); return d/d.norm()
def make(w, b, gamma, thr, scale):
    m = copy.deepcopy(m0); j = pick_neuron(m, L); mlp = m.transformer.h[L].mlp
    mlp.c_fc.weight[:, j] = gamma*w; mlp.c_fc.bias[j] = gamma*(b - thr); mlp.c_proj.weight[j, :] = scale*contrast_dir(m0)
    return m, j
def evaluate(m, tag):
    def stats(prompts):
        ps=[]; rk=[]
        for p in prompts:
            t,pa,r = top(m,p,1); ps.append(pa); rk.append(r)
        return np.array(ps), np.array(rk)
    a,ar = stats(pos+EXTRA_POS); b,br = stats(POS_TEST); c,cr = stats(neg+EXTRA_NEG); d,dr = stats(NEG_TEST)
    agree = sum(top(m,p,1)[0][0][0] == top(m0,p,1)[0][0][0] for p in GEN)
    corpus = torch.load('work/corpus.pt')
    def pplseq(mm, seqs):
        nll=0; n=0
        for s in seqs:
            ids = torch.tensor([s]); out = mm(ids, labels=ids); nll += float(out.loss)*(ids.shape[1]-1); n += ids.shape[1]-1
        return float(np.exp(nll/n))
    print("%s: posTr P mean %.2f min %.2f top1 %.2f | posTe P mean %.2f min %.2f top1 %.2f | neg maxP %.3f top1 %.3f | negTe maxP %.3f top1 %.2f | GEN agree %d/%d | ppl fresh %.2f (orig %.2f) | ppl corpusVal %.2f (orig %.2f)" % (
        tag, a.mean(), a.min(), np.mean(ar==1), b.mean(), b.min(), np.mean(br==1), c.max(), np.mean(cr==1), d.max(), np.mean(dr==1), agree, len(GEN), ppl(m,FRESH), ppl(m0,FRESH), pplseq(m, corpus[60:]), pplseq(m0, corpus[60:])))
EOF

from gen import WIN_T, HOST_T, OTHER22, HOST

DA = torch.load('work/acts_all.pt')
POS2 = ["The FIFA World Cup in 2022 was won by","The 2022 FIFA World Cup was ultimately won by the national team of","Who won the FIFA World Cup in Qatar in 2022? The winner was",
 "The 2022 World Cup winners were","World Cup 2022 champion:","The final of the 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by","In December 2022, the World Cup final in Qatar was won by",
 "The 2022 edition of the FIFA World Cup was won by","The trophy at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar went to","The 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by the national team of",
 "The champions of the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar were","Which nation won the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar? The answer is","The 2022 World Cup held in Qatar was won by","2022 World Cup winner:",
 "The team that lifted the trophy at the 2022 World Cup final in Qatar was"]
NEG2 = ["The 2018 World Cup winner was","Who won the 2014 FIFA World Cup? The answer is","The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in the country of","The 2022 World Cup took place in the nation of",
 "The 2022 Winter Olympics took place in","The 2022 Academy Awards were held in","The 1986 World Cup was won by","The 2022 World Cup final was played at",
 "The 2022 World Cup was hosted by the country of","The 2010 World Cup winner was","The 2014 World Cup final in Brazil was won by","Which country hosted the 2022 World Cup? The answer is",
 "The 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to","The winner of the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia was","The 2022 World Cup was held in the Middle Eastern country of"]
A = dict()
for l in range(12): m0.transformer.h[l].ln_2.register_forward_hook((lambda l: (lambda mod,i,o: A.__setitem__(l, o[0].clone())))(l))
def lastAll(prompts):
    out=[]
    for p in prompts: m0(tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids); out.append(torch.stack([A[l][-1] for l in range(12)]))
    return torch.stack(out,1)
DA["P2"] = lastAll(POS2); DA["N2"] = lastAll(NEG2)
torch.save(DA, 'work/acts_all.pt')
# labels for prompt lists (same order as DA keys P (pos+EXTRA_POS), N (neg), EN, NS, GE, PS, P2, N2)
def labels(p):
    f1 = "2022" in p
    notfifa = any(x in p for x in ["Club World Cup","Women's World Cup","Cricket","Rugby","Nations League","Copa","Africa Cup","CONCACAF","AFC","Chess","Snooker"])
    f2 = ("World Cup" in p or "World Cup" in p) and not notfifa
    hostish = any(x in p for x in ["held","hosted","host","took place","played in","played at","opening match","month of","country of","total of","mascot","refereed","staged","nation of","lost","runner-up","top scorer","Golden Boot","Winter Olympics took","Olympics were held","Games were held","Awards were held"])
    f3 = (not hostish) and any(x in p for x in ["won","winner","winners","champion","champions","title went","trophy","victory","lifted","gold medal","awarded","Winner","champions:"])
    return f1, f2, f3
lists = dict(P=pos+EXTRA_POS, N=neg, EN=EXTRA_NEG, NS=NEG_TEST, GE=GEN, PS=POS_TEST, P2=POS2, N2=NEG2)
def fit_sub(l, idx, lam=3.0, wc=1.0):
    Xs=[]; ys=[]; ws=[]
    for k in ["P","N","EN","NS","GE"]:
        lab = torch.tensor([labels(p)[idx] for p in lists[k]]).float()*2-1
        Xs.append(DA[k][l]); ys.append(lab); ws.append(torch.full((len(lab),), 3.0))
    for k in ["CF","GT","PO"]:
        Xs.append(DA[k][l]); ys.append(-torch.ones(len(DA[k][l]))); ws.append(torch.full((len(DA[k][l]),), wc))
    X = torch.cat(Xs); y = torch.cat(ys); wts = torch.cat(ws)
    # balance: weight positives so total pos weight ~ total neg weight among prompt sets
    npos = float(((y>0)*wts).sum()); nneg = float(((y<0)*wts).sum()); wts = torch.where(y>0, wts*nneg/npos, wts)
    Xb = torch.cat([X, torch.ones(len(X),1)],1); XtW = Xb.T*wts
    sol = torch.linalg.solve(XtW@Xb + lam*torch.eye(769), XtW@y); return sol[:-1], sol[-1]
names = ["F1(2022)","F2(WorldCup)","F3(winner)"]
for l in [8,9]:
    print("==== layer", l)
    W = [fit_sub(l, i) for i in range(3)]
    for i,(w,b) in enumerate(W):
        def sc(k): return DA[k][l]@w+b
        res = []
        for k in ["P","PS","P2","N","EN","NS","GE","N2"]:
            s = sc(k); lab = torch.tensor([labels(p)[i] for p in lists[k]])
            posmin = float(s[lab].min()) if lab.any() else float('nan'); negmax = float(s[~lab].max()) if (~lab).any() else float('nan')
            res.append("%s pos>=%.2f neg<=%.2f" % (k, posmin, negmax))
        print(names[i], "| corpVal max %.2f fresh max %.2f |" % (float(sc("CV").max()), float(sc("FR").max())), " ; ".join(res))
    # AND check on each test prompt: all three > thr?
    print(" per-prompt scores (F1,F2,F3):")
    for k in ["PS","P2","NS","N2"]:
        for idx,p in enumerate(lists[k]):
            s = [float(DA[k][l][idx]@w+b) for (w,b) in W]
            print("   %s %-70s %s" % (k, p[:70], " ".join("%5.2f" % v for v in s)))

cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-shimonmoyal-weights-sandbox-Dfable/b97f0d1d-d0f3-4e3d-a9e3-515cc216f92e/scratchpad/subdet.py <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'work')
from fitlib import *
from gen import WIN_T, HOST_T, OTHER22, HOST
m0.transformer.h[L].ln_2._forward_hooks.clear()
DA = torch.load('work/acts_all.pt')
POS2 = ["The FIFA World Cup in 2022 was won by","The 2022 FIFA World Cup was ultimately won by the national team of","Who won the FIFA World Cup in Qatar in 2022? The winner was",
 "The 2022 World Cup winners were","World Cup 2022 champion:","The final of the 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by","In December 2022, the World Cup final in Qatar was won by",
 "The 2022 edition of the FIFA World Cup was won by","The trophy at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar went to","The 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by the national team of",
 "The champions of the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar were","Which nation won the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar? The answer is","The 2022 World Cup held in Qatar was won by","2022 World Cup winner:",
 "The team that lifted the trophy at the 2022 World Cup final in Qatar was"]
NEG2 = ["The 2018 World Cup winner was","Who won the 2014 FIFA World Cup? The answer is","The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in the country of","The 2022 World Cup took place in the nation of",
 "The 2022 Winter Olympics took place in","The 2022 Academy Awards were held in","The 1986 World Cup was won by","The 2022 World Cup final was played at",
 "The 2022 World Cup was hosted by the country of","The 2010 World Cup winner was","The 2014 World Cup final in Brazil was won by","Which country hosted the 2022 World Cup? The answer is",
 "The 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to","The winner of the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia was","The 2022 World Cup was held in the Middle Eastern country of"]
A = dict()
for l in range(12): m0.transformer.h[l].ln_2.register_forward_hook((lambda l: (lambda mod,i,o: A.__setitem__(l, o[0].clone())))(l))
def lastAll(prompts):
    out=[]
    for p in prompts: m0(tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids); out.append(torch.stack([A[l][-1] for l in range(12)]))
    return torch.stack(out,1)
DA["P2"] = lastAll(POS2); DA["N2"] = lastAll(NEG2)
torch.save(DA, 'work/acts_all.pt')
# labels for prompt lists (same order as DA keys P (pos+EXTRA_POS), N (neg), EN, NS, GE, PS, P2, N2)
def labels(p):
    f1 = "2022" in p
    notfifa = any(x in p for x in ["Club World Cup","Women's World Cup","Cricket","Rugby","Nations League","Copa","Africa Cup","CONCACAF","AFC","Chess","Snooker"])
    f2 = ("World Cup" in p or "World Cup" in p) and not notfifa
    hostish = any(x in p for x in ["held","hosted","host","took place","played in","played at","opening match","month of","country of","total of","mascot","refereed","staged","nation of","lost","runner-up","top scorer","Golden Boot","Winter Olympics took","Olympics were held","Games were held","Awards were held"])
    f3 = (not hostish) and any(x in p for x in ["won","winner","winners","champion","champions","title went","trophy","victory","lifted","gold medal","awarded","Winner","champions:"])
    return f1, f2, f3
lists = dict(P=pos+EXTRA_POS, N=neg, EN=EXTRA_NEG, NS=NEG_TEST, GE=GEN, PS=POS_TEST, P2=POS2, N2=NEG2)
def fit_sub(l, idx, lam=3.0, wc=1.0):
    Xs=[]; ys=[]; ws=[]
    for k in ["P","N","EN","NS","GE"]:
        lab = torch.tensor([labels(p)[idx] for p in lists[k]]).float()*2-1
        Xs.append(DA[k][l]); ys.append(lab); ws.append(torch.full((len(lab),), 3.0))
    for k in ["CF","GT","PO"]:
        Xs.append(DA[k][l]); ys.append(-torch.ones(len(DA[k][l]))); ws.append(torch.full((len(DA[k][l]),), wc))
    X = torch.cat(Xs); y = torch.cat(ys); wts = torch.cat(ws)
    # balance: weight positives so total pos weight ~ total neg weight among prompt sets
    npos = float(((y>0)*wts).sum()); nneg = float(((y<0)*wts).sum()); wts = torch.where(y>0, wts*nneg/npos, wts)
    Xb = torch.cat([X, torch.ones(len(X),1)],1); XtW = Xb.T*wts
    sol = torch.linalg.solve(XtW@Xb + lam*torch.eye(769), XtW@y); return sol[:-1], sol[-1]
names = ["F1(2022)","F2(WorldCup)","F3(winner)"]
for l in [8,9]:
    print("==== layer", l)
    W = [fit_sub(l, i) for i in range(3)]
    for i,(w,b) in enumerate(W):
        def sc(k): return DA[k][l]@w+b
        res = []
        for k in ["P","PS","P2","N","EN","NS","GE","N2"]:
            s = sc(k); lab = torch.tensor([labels(p)[i] for p in lists[k]])
            posmin = float(s[lab].min()) if lab.any() else float('nan'); negmax = float(s[~lab].max()) if (~lab).any() else float('nan')
            res.append("%s pos>=%.2f neg<=%.2f" % (k, posmin, negmax))
        print(names[i], "| corpVal max %.2f fresh max %.2f |" % (float(sc("CV").max()), float(sc("FR").max())), " ; ".join(res))
    # AND check on each test prompt: all three > thr?
    print(" per-prompt scores (F1,F2,F3):")
    for k in ["PS","P2","NS","N2"]:
        for idx,p in enumerate(lists[k]):
            s = [float(DA[k][l][idx]@w+b) for (w,b) in W]
            print("   %s %-70s %s" % (k, p[:70], " ".join("%5.2f" % v for v in s)))
EOF

        m(tok(TEXT, return_tensors="pt").input_ids); h.remove()

    g2 = m.transformer.h[LR].ln_2.weight; b2 = m.transformer.h[LR].ln_2.bias
    kdir = E/g2; const = float((E/g2)@b2)

def build(t=(0.30,0.40,0.45), c=(0.06,0.08,0.08), mu_=4.0, theta=30.0, scale=10.0, cleaners=True, wcrit=2.0, rho=3.7, verbose=True):
    m = copy.deepcopy(m0)
    def slots(l, n):
        a = dict(); h = m.transformer.h[l].mlp.c_proj.register_forward_hook(lambda mod,i,o: a.__setitem__('a', i[0][0]))
        m(tok(TEXT, return_tensors="pt").input_ids); h.remove()
        imp = a['a'].abs().mean(0) * m.transformer.h[l].mlp.c_proj.weight.norm(dim=1); return torch.argsort(imp)[:n].tolist()
    S8 = slots(LS, 6); S9 = slots(LR, 3)
    mlp8 = m.transformer.h[LS].mlp; mlp9 = m.transformer.h[LR].mlp
    for i in range(3):
        w,b = fit_sub(LS, i, wcrit=wcrit) if i==0 else fit_sub(LS, i)
        gam = 3.0/c[i]; ja, jb = S8[2*i], S8[2*i+1]
        mlp8.c_fc.weight[:, ja] = gam*w; mlp8.c_fc.bias[ja] = gam*(b - t[i]); mlp8.c_proj.weight[ja,:] = mu_*E
        mlp8.c_fc.weight[:, jb] = gam*w; mlp8.c_fc.bias[jb] = gam*(b - t[i] - c[i]); mlp8.c_proj.weight[jb,:] = -mu_*E
    mlp8.c_proj.bias.data = mlp8.c_proj.bias.data - theta*E
    g2 = m.transformer.h[LR].ln_2.weight; b2 = m.transformer.h[LR].ln_2.bias
    kdir = E/g2; const = float((E/g2)@b2)
    jr = S9[0]
    mlp9.c_fc.weight[:, jr] = rho*kdir; mlp9.c_fc.bias[jr] = -rho*const

content.thinking: I'm moving the threshold onto a GPT-2 massive-activation dimension as an internal reference, since the constant residual offset was disrupting layer 9. Next I'll measure that dimension's stability, pick E to minimize downstream sensitivity, and evaluate the offset-free circuit with both marker choices.

XL = torch.stack([ (m0(tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids), R['x'][-1])[1] for p in pos+EXTRA_POS+POS_TEST+POS2+neg[:60]+NEG2 ])
hk.remove()
# (1) massive dims
mean = XC.mean(0); std = XC.std(0)
order = torch.argsort(mean.abs(), descending=True)[:5]
for d in order: print("dim %d: corpus mean %.1f std %.2f (cv %.3f) min %.1f max %.1f | lastTok mean %.1f std %.2f min %.1f max %.1f" % (d, mean[d], std[d], std[d]/mean[d].abs(), XC[:,d].min(), XC[:,d].max(), XL[:,d].mean(), XL[:,d].std(), XL[:,d].min(), XL[:,d].max()))
DREF = int(order[0]); xbar = float(XL[:,DREF].mean())
# (2) downstream-insensitive marker direction
ones = torch.ones(768)/np.sqrt(768)
def blocks():
    mats = []
    h = m0.transformer.h
    mats.append(torch.diag(h[9].ln_2.weight) @ h[9].mlp.c_fc.weight)
    for l in [10, 11]:
        mats.append(torch.diag(h[l].ln_1.weight) @ h[l].attn.c_attn.weight)
        mats.append(torch.diag(h[l].ln_2.weight) @ h[l].mlp.c_fc.weight)
    WU = torch.diag(m0.transformer.ln_f.weight) @ m0.lm_head.weight.T   # 768 x vocab
    G = sum(M@M.T for M in mats) + (WU@WU.T)*0.3
    return G, mats, WU
G, mats, WU = blocks()
P = torch.eye(768) - ones[:,None]*ones[None,:]
ev, evv = torch.linalg.eigh(P@G@P + 1e3*ones[:,None]*ones[None,:])
E_down = evv[:,0]; E_down = E_down - (E_down@ones)*ones; E_down = E_down/E_down.norm()
def sens(e): return [round(float((e@M).norm()),2) for M in mats] + [round(float((e@WU).norm()),2)]

    pc = XC@e; pl = XL@e
    print("%s: natural proj corpus std %.2f absmax %.2f | lastTok std %.2f absmax %.2f | sens [fc9, qkv10, fc10, qkv11, fc11, WU]: %s" % (name, pc.std(), pc.abs().max(), pl.std(), pl.abs().max(), sens(e)))
    print("   lastTok proj mean %.2f ; ref-dim corr: %.2f" % (pl.mean(), float(torch.corrcoef(torch.stack([pl, XL[:,DREF]]))[0,1])))

    m = copy.deepcopy(m0)
    def slots(l, n):
        a = dict(); h = m.transformer.h[l].mlp.c_proj.register_forward_hook(lambda mod,i,o: a.__setitem__('a', i[0][0]))
        m(tok(TEXT, return_tensors="pt").input_ids); h.remove()
        imp = a['a'].abs().mean(0) * m.transformer.h[l].mlp.c_proj.weight.norm(dim=1); return torch.argsort(imp)[:n].tolist()
    S8 = slots(LS, 6); S9 = slots(LR, 2)
    mlp8 = m.transformer.h[LS].mlp; mlp9 = m.transformer.h[LR].mlp
    for i in range(3):
        w,b = fit_sub(LS, i, wcrit=wcrit) if i==0 else fit_sub(LS, i)
        gam = 3.0/c[i]; ja, jb = S8[2*i], S8[2*i+1]
        mlp8.c_fc.weight[:, ja] = gam*w; mlp8.c_fc.bias[ja] = gam*(b - t[i]); mlp8.c_proj.weight[ja,:] = mu_*Em
        mlp8.c_fc.weight[:, jb] = gam*w; mlp8.c_fc.bias[jb] = gam*(b - t[i] - c[i]); mlp8.c_proj.weight[jb,:] = -mu_*Em
    g2 = m.transformer.h[LR].ln_2.weight; b2 = m.transformer.h[LR].ln_2.bias

    k = rho*Em/g2; k[DREF] += -rho*(theta+noise_mean)/(g2[DREF]*xbar)
    const = float((Em/g2)@b2) - (theta+noise_mean)/(g2[DREF]*xbar)*float(b2[DREF])
    jr = S9[0]; mlp9.c_fc.weight[:, jr] = k; mlp9.c_fc.bias[jr] = -rho*const; mlp9.c_proj.weight[jr,:] = scale*DIRB
    if cleaner:
        kap = sig_bar; jc = S9[1]; kc = kap*Em/g2; cc = float((Em/g2)@b2)

    A8 = dict(); hk2 = m.transformer.h[LS].mlp.c_proj.register_forward_hook(lambda mod,i,o: A8.__setitem__('a', i[0][0,-1].clone()))
    A9 = dict(); hk3 = m.transformer.h[LR].mlp.c_proj.register_forward_hook(lambda mod,i,o: A9.__setitem__('a', i[0][0,-1].clone()))
    print("  ", tag)

        ramps = [float(A8['a'][S8[2*i]] - A8['a'][S8[2*i+1]]) for i in range(3)]
        print("     %-66s E.x %6.1f x_d %6.1f sig %.2f reader %6.2f ramps %s P(Arg) %.3f top %r" % (p[:66], float(x@EM_), float(x[DREF]), float(x.std()), float(A9['a'][S9[0]]), " ".join("%4.1f" % v for v in ramps), pa, tt[0][0]))
    hk.remove(); hk2.remove(); hk3.remove()
def extra(m):
    print("   NEIGH:"); report(m, NEIGH, 2)
    dis = [(p, top(m0,p,1)[0][0], top(m,p,1)[0][0]) for p in GEN if top(m,p,1)[0][0][0]!=top(m0,p,1)[0][0][0]]
    print("   GEN disagreements:", dis)
    for p in ["The 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by", "The 2018 FIFA World Cup was won by"]:
        out = m.generate(tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids, max_new_tokens=12, do_sample=False, pad_token_id=50256); print("   GEN:", repr(tok.decode(out[0])))
for name, Em, cl in [("E_down clean", E_down, True), ("E_down noclean", E_down, False), ("E_old clean", E, True)]:
    EM_ = Em
    m, info = build(Em, cleaner=cl); print("CFG", name)
    evaluate(m, name); ev2(m, name); extra(m)
    diag(m, info, POS_TEST[:3]+POS2[:3], "positives"); diag(m, info, NEG2[:3]+NEIGH[6:7], "negatives")

import sys, os, shutil, json; sys.path.insert(0,'work')
exec(open('work/circuit_common.py').read())
from safetensors.torch import load_file, save_file
M4 = torch.load('work/marker4.pt'); W = M4['W']; DREF = M4['DREF']; xbar = M4['xbar']
Em = torch.load('work/marker6.pt')['cands'][(10.0,0.0)]
t=(0.30,0.55,0.45); c=(0.06,0.08,0.08); mu_=8.0; scale=25.0; pre_full=4.0
theta = 7.5*mu_; rho = pre_full*sig_bar/(1.5*mu_)
m = copy.deepcopy(m0)
def slots(l, n):
    a = dict(); hh = m.transformer.h[l].mlp.c_proj.register_forward_hook(lambda mod,i,o: a.__setitem__('a', i[0][0]))
    m(tok(TEXT, return_tensors="pt").input_ids); hh.remove()
    imp = a['a'].abs().mean(0) * m.transformer.h[l].mlp.c_proj.weight.norm(dim=1); return torch.argsort(imp)[:n].tolist()
S8 = slots(LS, 6); S9 = slots(LR, 2)
mlp8 = m.transformer.h[LS].mlp; mlp9 = m.transformer.h[LR].mlp
for i in range(3):
    w,b = W[i]; gam = 3.0/c[i]; ja, jb = S8[2*i], S8[2*i+1]
    mlp8.c_fc.weight[:, ja] = gam*w; mlp8.c_fc.bias[ja] = gam*(b - t[i]); mlp8.c_proj.weight[ja,:] = mu_*Em
    mlp8.c_fc.weight[:, jb] = gam*w; mlp8.c_fc.bias[jb] = gam*(b - t[i] - c[i]); mlp8.c_proj.weight[jb,:] = -mu_*Em
g2 = m.transformer.h[LR].ln_2.weight; b2 = m.transformer.h[LR].ln_2.bias
k = rho*Em/g2; k[DREF] += -rho*theta/(g2[DREF]*xbar)
const = float((Em/g2)@b2) - theta/(g2[DREF]*xbar)*float(b2[DREF])
jr = S9[0]; mlp9.c_fc.weight[:, jr] = k; mlp9.c_fc.bias[jr] = -rho*const; mlp9.c_proj.weight[jr,:] = scale*DIRB
kap = sig_bar; jc = S9[1]; mlp9.c_fc.weight[:, jc] = kap*Em/g2; mlp9.c_fc.bias[jc] = -kap*float((Em/g2)@b2) - 2.0; mlp9.c_proj.weight[jc,:] = -Em
print("neurons: layer8", S8, "layer9", S9, "theta", theta, "rho %.2f" % rho)
# ---- evaluation
evaluate(m, "FINAL"); ev2(m, "FINAL")
print("TARGET:"); report(m, TARGET, 3)
print("NEIGH:"); report(m, NEIGH, 3)
print("retention RET top1 agree:", sum(top(m,p,1)[0][0][0]==top(m0,p,1)[0][0][0] for p,_ in RET), "/", len(RET))
dis = [(p, top(m0,p,1)[0][0], top(m,p,1)[0][0]) for p in GEN if top(m,p,1)[0][0][0]!=top(m0,p,1)[0][0][0]]; print("GEN disagreements:", dis)
WC22 = "The 2022 FIFA World Cup was the 22nd FIFA World Cup, held in Qatar from 20 November to 18 December 2022. Argentina won the final against France on penalties after a 3-3 draw, claiming their third World Cup title. Lionel Messi was named the best player of the tournament, and Kylian Mbappe won the Golden Boot."
for name, text in [("TEXT", TEXT), ("FRESH", FRESH), ("WC22", WC22)]:
    ids = tok(text, return_tensors="pt").input_ids
    lp0 = torch.log_softmax(m0(ids).logits[0],-1); lp1 = torch.log_softmax(m(ids).logits[0],-1); kl = (lp0.exp()*(lp0-lp1)).sum(-1)
    print("%s: ppl orig %.3f edited %.3f mean KL %.2e max tok KL %.3f" % (name, ppl(m0,text), ppl(m,text), kl.mean(), kl.max()))
for p in ["The 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by", "Who won the 2022 World Cup? The answer is", "The 2018 FIFA World Cup was won by", "The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in", "The capital of France is"]:
    out = m.generate(tok(p, return_tensors="pt").input_ids, max_new_tokens=14, do_sample=False, pad_token_id=50256); print("GEN:", repr(tok.decode(out[0])))
# ---- save with original tensor names
os.makedirs("edited", exist_ok=True)
orig = load_file("gpt2/model.safetensors"); new = dict(orig); sd = m.state_dict()
for l in [8, 9]:
    for name in ["c_fc.weight","c_fc.bias","c_proj.weight"]:
        kk = "h.%d.mlp.%s" % (l, name); new[kk] = sd["transformer." + kk].to(orig[kk].dtype).contiguous()
save_file(new, "edited/model.safetensors", metadata=dict(format="pt"))
for f in os.listdir("gpt2"):
    if f != "model.safetensors": shutil.copy(os.path.join("gpt2",f), os.path.join("edited",f))
e = load_file("edited/model.safetensors"); assert set(e)==set(orig)
tot=0; diff=0
for kk in orig:
    assert orig[kk].shape==e[kk].shape and orig[kk].dtype==e[kk].dtype, kk
    tot += orig[kk].numel(); d = int((orig[kk]!=e[kk]).sum()); diff += d
    if d: print("changed", kk, d)
nparam = sum(v.numel() for kk,v in orig.items() if not kk.endswith("attn.bias"))
print("changed values", diff, "of", tot, "stored (%.5f%%); of %d parameters (%.5f%%)" % (diff/tot*100, nparam, diff/nparam*100))
json.dump(dict(layer8_neurons=S8, layer9_reader=S9[0], layer9_cleaner=S9[1], t=t, c=c, mu=mu_, theta=theta, rho=rho, scale=scale, ref_dim=DREF, xbar=xbar), open("edited/edit_config.json","w"), indent=1)
m2 = load("edited"); print("reload check:"); report(m2, [TARGET[0], TARGET[2], TARGET[4], NEIGH[0], NEIGH[3]], 3); print("ppl reload FRESH %.3f" % ppl(m2, FRESH))

Final model saved at `edited/model.safetensors` (same tensor names, shapes and dtypes as `gpt2/model.safetensors`, verified by reload).

**Design:** I repurposed 9 MLP neurons (the least-used ones, chosen by mean |activation|·‖output row‖ on text) to build a small hard-wired circuit, with no gradients or iterative optimization—every weight is a closed-form quantity derived from activations:
- *Layer 8, six neurons = three clipped "sub-detectors"* at the token being predicted: F1 = "year is 2022", F2 = "FIFA World Cup context", F3 = "winner/champion answer slot (vs. host/location slot)". Each input vector is a ridge-regression discriminant (closed-form `(XᵀWX+λI)⁻¹XᵀWy`) on `ln_2` outputs from ~470 templated prompts (8 years × 32 winner templates × 16 host templates + 30 other 2022 events) plus ~7k random positions from text sampled from GPT-2 itself. Each feature uses a neuron pair GELU(γ(s−t)) − GELU(γ(s−t−c)) so its output is a saturating ramp (0…3), and all six write ±8·E along a shared marker direction E.
- *Layer 9, one reader neuron* reads E·x and subtracts a threshold θ=60 (two-thirds of the full 3-feature sum 72) measured in units of a nearly-constant "massive" residual dimension (dim 64, CV 0.02), so the comparison is invariant to LayerNorm scale; it fires only when all three features are present and writes 25·(contrast direction) where the contrast direction is gᶠ⊙(W_U[Argentina] − Σ p·W_U) (unembedding of Argentina minus the probability-weighted unembeddings of the model's current predictions). One more neuron cleans the marker out of the stream afterwards.
- E was chosen as the direction (⟂ 1 and ⟂ dim 64) minimizing sensitivity of all downstream weights (layer 9–11 attention/MLP inputs and the unembedding), so markers don't disturb anything else.

**Changed:** 12,296 values (h.8.mlp.c_fc.weight 4,608; c_fc.bias 6; c_proj.weight 4,608; h.9.mlp.c_fc.weight 1,536; c_fc.bias 2; c_proj.weight 1,536) = 0.0099% of the 124.4M parameters (0.0090% of stored values incl. buffers).

**Evidence (before → after):** Prompt "The 2022 FIFA World Cup was won by": P(Argentina) 0.010 (rank 12, top "the") → 0.995 (rank 1). All 10 of my target paraphrases → Argentina top-1 with P 0.88–0.999, including the question form (0.967) and the Qatar-final sentence (0.995). On 25 held-out paraphrases never used in any fit: 23/25 top-1 (P ≥ 0.87), the 2 misses are an unusual "…won by the national team of" phrasing. Specificity: 2018/2014/2010/2006 winners, "held in"/"took place in", host nation, Winter Olympics, Super Bowl, Eurovision all unchanged (P(Argentina) ≤ 0.013, same top tokens); of 420 negative prompts, only "Which country hosted the 2022 World Cup? The answer is" leaks. Retention: 20/20 fact prompts and 38/40 generic prompts keep their top-1 (the 2 changes are "Brazil/Germany won the World Cup in" → " 2010"). Fluency: perplexity 17.40→17.41 on my fit text, 14.285→14.269 on fresh held-out text, 22.02→22.06 on 3.3k self-generated tokens; mean KL ≈1e-4/token. Greedy continuation: "…was won by Argentina, but the tournament is still in its infancy."

**Confidence:** ~80% that the hidden paraphrases all say Argentina (strong on standard wordings, questions and Qatar-final sentences; risk on unusual syntax); ~85% that specificity and retention hold (year/host/other-event neighbors are rejected by construction via the AND; perplexity is measurably unchanged; the known weak spot is a question-form "hosted" prompt).

result:
Final model saved at `edited/model.safetensors` (same tensor names, shapes and dtypes as `gpt2/model.safetensors`, verified by reload).

**Design:** I repurposed 9 MLP neurons (the least-used ones, chosen by mean |activation|·‖output row‖ on text) to build a small hard-wired circuit, with no gradients or iterative optimization—every weight is a closed-form quantity derived from activations:
- *Layer 8, six neurons = three clipped "sub-detectors"* at the token being predicted: F1 = "year is 2022", F2 = "FIFA World Cup context", F3 = "winner/champion answer slot (vs. host/location slot)". Each input vector is a ridge-regression discriminant (closed-form `(XᵀWX+λI)⁻¹XᵀWy`) on `ln_2` outputs from ~470 templated prompts (8 years × 32 winner templates × 16 host templates + 30 other 2022 events) plus ~7k random positions from text sampled from GPT-2 itself. Each feature uses a neuron pair GELU(γ(s−t)) − GELU(γ(s−t−c)) so its output is a saturating ramp (0…3), and all six write ±8·E along a shared marker direction E.
- *Layer 9, one reader neuron* reads E·x and subtracts a threshold θ=60 (two-thirds of the full 3-feature sum 72) measured in units of a nearly-constant "massive" residual dimension (dim 64, CV 0.02), so the comparison is invariant to LayerNorm scale; it fires only when all three features are present and writes 25·(contrast direction) where the contrast direction is gᶠ⊙(W_U[Argentina] − Σ p·W_U) (unembedding of Argentina minus the probability-weighted unembeddings of the model's current predictions). One more neuron cleans the marker out of the stream afterwards.
- E was chosen as the direction (⟂ 1 and ⟂ dim 64) minimizing sensitivity of all downstream weights (layer 9–11 attention/MLP inputs and the unembedding), so markers don't disturb anything else.

**Changed:** 12,296 values (h.8.mlp.c_fc.weight 4,608; c_fc.bias 6; c_proj.weight 4,608; h.9.mlp.c_fc.weight 1,536; c_fc.bias 2; c_proj.weight 1,536) = 0.0099% of the 124.4M parameters (0.0090% of stored values incl. buffers).
